title: [BUG] Consider disabling managed memory in cudf.pandas on WSL2
body_excerpt: **Describe the bug** cudf.pandas turns on a managed pool allocator by default to support larger-than-memory workloads. However, this does not work on WSL2 because UVM on Windows does not actually allow oversubscription. Moreover, using UVM could result in far worse slowdowns on WSL2 than observed on Windows due to how it is implemented on that platform.  **Expected behavior** We should consider changing cudf.pandas to only enable managed memory by default when oversubscription is properly supported. This can be done by querying the CUDA driver for the appropriate attribute. In addition, we should run some benchmarks to evaluate the relative performance impact of using managed memory on WSL2 in undersubscribed situations

title: Pass NULL pointer for cffi.FFI().from_buffer(empty array)
body_excerpt: When linking to a C function from the python CUDA kernel, the data in a device array can be passed by the expression ``` ffi.from_buffer(d_ary) ```  However, an exception if raised if an empty array is passed. This should instead be passed as a `NULL` pointer. There is not the danger of dereferencing a `NULL` pointer as the size of the array must also be passed to the C function.

title: CUDA; Need to handle incorrect `CUDA_HOME` more gracefully
body_excerpt: It looks like Numba doesn't handle it very gracefully when `CUDA_HOME` is incorrectly set (see traceback in report for #9216). We can improve on the feedback to the user:  *  It would be much better if it made it clear that `CUDA_HOME` was not correct rather than giving the exception stating that NVVM is missing * When `CUDA_HOME` is set incorrectly, the CUDA libraries test raises an exception and therefore `numba -s` prints no helpful information about the failure to detect components of the toolkit * `CUDA_HOME` should also be included in the list of relevant environment variables affecting Numba.  cc @AromaticJ
